newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on profit taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Monday amid some profit taking, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 0.21 percent, or 0.64 points, to 304.28 on all-share turnover of 195 million shekels against 202 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.38 percent lower at 311.58.

"The market made a nice move and investors are now taking profits. The market is still very strong and activity is rising. The fact that after such a sharp rise the market is declining by less than 0.5 percent shows the mood is very positive," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"This is only a technical correction. The market rose for four consecutive sessions and today investors took profits," said Izik Winish at Capital Securities.

"The indicators are very good. The mutual funds continue to raise new money, the new offerings are very successful and foreign investors are showing more interest in the Israeli market," the Hapoalim trader said.
Winish added that investors were also waiting for the Bank of Israel's decision on interest rates. "The market is bullish but investors prefer to wait another day until after the rate decision."
After the close of trading the Bank of Israel announced it would leave its key lending rate for August unchanged at an annual 12.7 percent.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.75 percent to 38,684 agorot (Israeli cents) on volume of 14.1 million shekels; Tadiran, which rose 3.25 percent to 11,946 agorot on turnover of 12.3 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 22,409 agorot on turnover of 8.45 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 DMG TCC
